newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia trade deficit narrows 13.3 pct Jan-April.
newsitem.headline: Colombia trade deficit narrows 13.3 pct Jan-April.

text.p: Colombia's trade deficit narrowed 13.3 percent to $600.6 million FOB in the first four months of the year as coffee exports jumped, the National Statistics Department said Thursday.
The deficit compares with a $692.6 million trade shortfall registered in the corresponding period in 1996. FOB, or "free on board," is used to value goods at point of embarkation

The year-over-year decline mainly reflected a surge in the value of coffee exports, which climbed 27.1 percent to $604.8 million from January through April. Shipments of oil and oil derivatives rose 7 percent to $920.6 million.

Colombia's total exports grew 5.8 percent to $3.54 billion FOB in the first four months of 1997. Traditional exports such as coffee and oil grew 13.1 percent to $1.85 billion in terms of value and 9.9 percent in terms of volume.

The value of non-traditional exports -- a category that consists of agricultural products, manufactured goods and some metals and minerals -- dropped 1.21 percent to $1.69 billion. When exports of gold and emeralds are factored out, non-traditional exports grew 3.52 percent.
Imports rose 2.3 percent to 44.43 billion CIF in the same period. CIF, or cost, insurance and freight, reflects the value of goods at point of entry after transport and insurance are paid.
